simple.meaning: תְּנוּךְ (tᵉnûwk) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a pinnacle , i.e. extremity.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 29:20. The surrounding context includes family line, offering, altar, blood, death, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּנוּךְ (H8571) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תְּנוּךְ (tᵉnûwk) / H8571 is traced through Exodus 29:20, Leviticus 8:23, Leviticus 8:24, Leviticus 14:14 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then you shall kill the ram, and take some of its blood, and put it on the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and on the tip of the right ear of his sons, and on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot; and sprinkle the blood around on the altar.

definitions.full: H8571. tenuk תְּנוּךְ noun [masculine] tip , i.e. lobe of ear ( ᵐ5 λοβὸς τοῦ ὠτός , ᵑ9 extremum auriculae , and so most ancient authorities, compare Thes 151l ); — construct in phrase ׳תּ פ ׳אֹזֶן Exod 29:20 (twice in verse); Lev 8:23-24 , 14:14 , 17 , 25 , 28 (all P). תְּנוּמָה see נום . תְּנוּפָה see I. נוף .
